original_value: AbstractThe Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) tree, encoding the generative process of an object by a recursive compositional structure of bounded primitives, constitutes an important structural representation of 3D objects. Therefore, automatically recovering such a compositional structure from the raw point cloud of an object represents a high‐level reverse engineering problem, finding applications from structure and functionality analysis to creative redesign. We propose an effective method to construct CSG models and trees directly over raw point clouds. Specifically, a large number of hypothetical bounded primitive candidates are first extracted from raw scans, followed by a carefully designed pruning strategy. We then choose to approximate the target CSG model by the combination of a subset of these candidates with corresponding Boolean operations using a binary optimization technique, from which the corresponding CSG tree can be derived. Our method attempts to consider the minimal description length concept in the point cloud analysis setting, where the objective function is designed to minimize the construction error and complexity simultaneously. We demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our method with extensive experiments on real scan data with various complexities and styles.

result.paraphrase: Abstract The Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) tree, which encodes an object's generative process through a recursive composition of bounded primitives, is a key structural representation for 3D objects. Accordingly, automatically reconstructing this compositional structure from an object's raw point cloud is a high-level reverse-engineering task with applications ranging from structure and functionality analysis to creative redesign. We present an effective approach for building CSG models and trees directly from raw point clouds. In particular, we first extract a large set of candidate bounded primitives from raw scans, then apply a carefully designed pruning strategy. Next, using a binary optimization technique, we approximate the target CSG model by combining a subset of these candidates with the corresponding Boolean operations, from which the associated CSG tree can be derived. Our method is designed to incorporate the minimal description length principle in point-cloud analysis, with an objective function that simultaneously minimizes construction error and complexity. Extensive experiments on real scan data with diverse complexities and styles demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our method.
